name: MonarchDeviceFrame
title: DeviceFrame
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box with Modifier.aspectRatio, Modifier.clip and Modifier.drawBehind
summary: A phone or tablet outline around a preview: a link page, an email, a mobile layout.
whenToUse: In builders and editors that show how something will look on a phone or a tablet: a link page, an email template, a mobile layout. Mostly on a tablet; on a phone the frame is smaller than the device.
whenNotToUse: To show a screenshot as a plain picture use an Image. To preview a live web page use the app's WebView screen without a frame.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchDeviceFrame(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, device: MonarchDeviceFrameDevice = MonarchDeviceFrameDevice.Phone, screenSize: DpSize? = null, statusBarTime: String? = null, interactive: Boolean = false, flat: Boolean = false, content: @Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)
public enum class MonarchDeviceFrameDevice { Phone, Tablet }

options.name: label
options.description: What the frame shows, for example "Preview of your link page on a phone". It names the preview for TalkBack.

options.name: device
options.description: Phone: 44dp corners, a 10dp bezel and a camera island. Tablet: 28dp corners, a 14dp bezel and no island.

options.name: screenSize
options.description: The width the frame never exceeds and, with the height, its aspect ratio. 390 by 844dp for a phone and 820 by 1180dp for a tablet by default.

options.name: statusBarTime
options.description: Shows a decorative status bar with this time text, for example "9:41".

options.name: interactive
options.description: Lets people scroll and use the content. Put a scrolling container in the content when it is taller than the screen.

options.name: flat
options.description: Leaves out the side buttons and the shadow, for dense layouts.

options.name: content
options.description: The screen content, laid out in the screen area and clipped to it.

states.name: preview
states.description: The default: the frame is one image for TalkBack and its content takes no touches and no keyboard focus.

states.name: interactive
states.description: The content keeps its own elements, touches and focus.

states.name: flat
states.description: No side buttons and no shadow.

appearance: The frame, the island and the side buttons use the inverse background, so the device stands out from the canvas in light, dark and both high-contrast themes; the screen uses the surface color with default text. The frame casts the xl shadow unless flat.
platformNotes: Dimensions follow the web and iOS: a 10dp bezel and 44dp corners for the phone, 14 and 28 for the tablet, screen sizes of 390 by 844 and 820 by 1180. The web takes separate width and height numbers; Android takes one DpSize, like iOS's CGSize. The frame scales to the width it is given and keeps its aspect ratio, but its content is not scaled, as on the web. The web's interactive frame scrolls its own content; here the app places a scrolling container in the content. Low priority on a phone.
accessibility: A frame that is not interactive is one TalkBack element with the image role, named by label; its content is removed from the accessibility tree, takes no touches and takes no keyboard focus.
An interactive frame is a traversal group named by label, and the elements of its content stay reachable and usable.
The island, the status bar and the side buttons are hidden from TalkBack.
The side buttons follow the layout direction: the volume buttons are on the start edge.
The status bar time grows with the font size setting; the bezel and the island do not.
edgeCases: In a container narrower than the screen size the frame shrinks and keeps the aspect ratio; content laid out for the full width may be clipped.
Content taller than the screen is clipped unless the frame is interactive and the content scrolls.
